- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is bullish (high sentiment scores) — adjust downward by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish (low sentiment scores) — add 1–3% to forecast for the first 3–5 days.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after a recent price spike — cap forecast growth at 3–5% above prior peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged forecast errors: if true outcome is >5% above forecast on day 10+, reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day for next 3–5 days.
- Sentiment-driven overshoot: if sentiment >0.65 and forecast >true outcome by >2%, reduce forecast by 0.5–1% for next 3 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate by 1–3% — apply a 1% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
